about: Track E staging for data/targets.json (proposal by the Track E evidence researcher; applied by the integrator, this branch never edits targets.json). Order: (1) add `sources`; (2) append `targets` (T-ENE-1..9, T-RHY-1..10, T-END-1..12); (3) log a protocolLog entry and take a new freeze, because new rows and new observer protocols change the protocol hash. Nothing here was run: no simulated value of any row has been seen. Roles are held-out unless stated. Three flags need a decision at registration: T-ENE-5 is encoded while the C8c lactation taper is on; T-RHY-1 and T-RHY-8 are encoded while the nest clock and the midday-rest and temperature rules are on; T-END-4, -10 and -11 become encoded if E4 wires those events straight into the states. New observer protocols named here and not yet in src/field: 'energy ledger (truth)', 'camera-trap proxy (truth)', and urine or endocrine proxies combined with party scans, phenology, agonism records and the patrol classifier. Evidence, access and what was not verified: docs/staging/e-sources.md.

targets.metric: Daily metabolisable energy intake of adult females
targets.definition: Mean over full-day focal follows of the energy ingested per day by an adult female (kcal/d), summed over feeding minutes by food type.

field.value: 2,479 ± 858 kcal/d (mean ± SD of days); same in drupe and fig months
field.n: days not stated; F(1,139) in the seasonal test
field.method: full-day focal follows; intake = minutes × g/min × kcal/g; fibre credited at 1.6 kcal/g

field.value: total expenditure 1,722 ± 363 kcal/d at 46.4 kg (doubly labelled water); scaled to 31-35 kg about 1,300-1,450 kcal/d (derived)
field.note: expenditure, not intake; shown because intake must equal expenditure in steady state

accept.basis: field mean ± 25% (one site, widened); the band is the field intake estimate, not the expenditure estimate

targets.notes: The field intake estimate is 1.5-1.9 times the expenditure that doubly labelled water implies for a female of Gombe or Mahale mass. A ledger that conserves energy may land below this band; that would be a finding about the field estimate or the model, not a reason to add a correction factor. Never set: intake rates per minute are inputs, daily intake is the outcome. How to measure: the observer follows a focal adult female from nest to nest, logs each feeding minute with its food type, and multiplies by the registered kcal/min of that food (the field method); also report the ledger truth (kcal absorbed) beside it.

targets.metric: Daily feeding time of adult females
targets.definition: Mean feeding minutes per full-day focal follow of an adult female.

field.value: 308.7 ± 85 min/d; 20% lower in drupe months than in fig months
field.n: days not stated; F(1,139) in the seasonal test

accept.basis: field mean ± 20% (one site, widened)

targets.notes: Shares its field value with T-ACT-1 (fitted), so it cannot count as independent validation; registered so that E1 reports minutes beside the share. How to measure: count the focal minutes scored feeding on full-day follows of adult females (existing focal protocol).

targets.metric: Daily dry-matter intake of adult females
targets.definition: Mean dry mass ingested per day by an adult female (g/d): feeding minutes by food type × dry g/min.

field.n: days not stated; F(1,139) in the seasonal test
field.method: full-day focal follows; g/min by food item

accept.basis: field mean ± 25% (one site, widened)

targets.notes: Tied to T-ENE-1 by the energy density of the diet (about 2.8 kcal per g dry matter overall, derived). How to measure: as T-ENE-1 with the registered dry g/min per food (ripe fruit 3.4, young leaves 2.1, pith 1.8).

targets.metric: Energy balance rises with fruit
targets.definition: Association between an individual's energy-balance reading (sampled as a urine proxy) and the fruit share of the diet or fruit availability in the same period, within individuals.

field.value: urinary C-peptide predicted by the amount of fruit and of preferred fruit in the diet
C-peptide rises with food availability in both sexes

accept.basis: positive within-individual association between the energy-balance reading and fruit availability (or fruit share of the diet)

targets.notes: C-peptide reflects recent energy balance (insulin output), not the size of the reserves. How to measure: sample each adult's net energy balance over the previous day (ledger truth: intake − expenditure) at simulated urinations and regress it on the observer's phenology index for the same month, with individual as a random factor.

targets.metric: Energy balance through lactation
targets.definition: Energy-balance reading of mothers by time since birth: months 0-6, 6-12 and 12-24, within mothers.

field.value: C-peptide depressed for about 6 months postpartum, then a net increase through the second year; cycling resumes only after sustained gain; lower profiles in poorer foraging areas

accept.basis: months 0-6 below the mother's own later level; net rise through year 2

targets.notes: ENCODED while the C8c lactation taper is on: its knots lactTaperStartY 0.5 and lactTaperEndY 2 were set from this study. Counts as validation only if E1 derives the cost of lactation from milk energy and infant demand without those knots; set encoded to false at registration only in that case. How to measure: as T-ENE-4, grouped by the age of the youngest unweaned offspring from the census.

targets.metric: Females' energy balance falls with males in the party
targets.definition: Association between a female's energy-balance reading and the number of adult males in her parties over the preceding day.

field.value: lower urinary C-peptide when females associate with more males; receptive females raise the number of males in parties

accept.basis: negative association

targets.notes: How to measure: pair each female sample with the mean number of adult males in her 15-min party scans over the previous day.

targets.metric: Males feed less on days with parous oestrous females
targets.definition: Male feeding minutes per follow day: days with a maximally swollen parous female in the party against days with no swollen female.

field.value: males fed less on days with oestrous parous females than on days without mating opportunities; the drop tracked aggression and copulation rates; no effect of rank

accept.basis: feeding time lower on days with a swollen parous female present

targets.notes: How to measure: existing focal feeding minutes, split by the party-scan record of swollen parous females on that day.

targets.metric: Daily energy expenditure of non-reproducing adults, scaled by mass
targets.definition: Total daily energy expenditure of adults that are neither pregnant nor lactating, divided by body mass^0.75 (kcal per kg^0.75 per day), mean over individuals.

field.population: Genus Pan, captive adults (27 chimpanzees, 8 bonobos)
field.value: females 96.9, males 102.2 kcal/kg^0.75/d (derived from 1,722 kcal/d at 46.4 kg and 2,145 kcal/d at 57.9 kg); activity level 1.4-1.5
captive and wild populations have similar expenditure; chimpanzees 2,386 kcal/d at 57.1 kg with an older equation

accept.basis: captive value −12% to an activity level of about 1.9 (68 × 1.9) for a wild animal

targets.notes: A physiological consistency check, not a behaviour. It fails if the inputs (resting rate, cost per metre, activity multipliers) do not add up to a primate-like budget. No doubly-labelled-water value exists for wild chimpanzees. How to measure: read each adult's kcal spent per day from the ledger (simulation truth), with its body mass; no observer sampling.

targets.metric: Feeding time and travel against fruit availability
targets.definition: Monthly feeding minutes per day and day range per adult against the phenology index.

field.value: feeding time 20% lower in drupe months; daily energy intake unchanged
in scarce periods the daily journey shortens and feeding time rises
when food is abundant, less feeding time and more energy spent

accept.basis: feeding time higher and day range not longer in low-fruit months; daily intake varies less than fruit availability

targets.notes: Related to T-RNG-5 and T-FOOD rows; registered here for the intake side. How to measure: existing focal activity and fixes by month, against the phenology transect index.

targets.metric: Active day (nest to nest)
targets.definition: Time from leaving the night nest to entering the next one, per follow day, by sex and reproductive state (hours).

field.value: 11 h 34 min (males), 10 h 57 min (lactating females)

accept.basis: the two Budongo values with a margin of about half an hour

targets.notes: Today the nest clock (nestEveningStartH, nestEveningEndH, nestWakeHour) sets this, so it is encoded until the E2 switch removes those rules; score it as validation only with the clock rules off. activeDayH (11.5 h) then stops being a parameter. How to measure: the observer records the tick a focal leaves its night nest and the tick it settles in the next one (nest state changes are already in the event log).

targets.metric: Active day by sex and reproductive state
targets.definition: Difference in active-day length between adult males, non-receptive females and receptive (swollen) females; females in dry against wet months.

field.value: non-receptive females shorter than males; receptive females longer than males; non-receptive females longer in the dry season; high- and middle-ranking males shorter than low-ranking males
lactating females 37 min shorter than males

accept.basis: non-receptive (lactating) females shorter than males; receptive females not shorter than males

targets.notes: No durations are in the Gombe abstract. How to measure: as T-RHY-1, grouped by sex and swelling state from the census.

targets.metric: Nest departures before sunrise
targets.definition: Share of morning nest departures of adult females that happen before sunrise.

field.value: 18% of departures before sunrise; earlier for ephemeral fruit (figs) and when the breakfast tree is farther

accept.basis: one site and one season type, widened

targets.notes: The dependence on fruit type and distance is a second, direction-only reading of the same row. How to measure: compare the departure tick of T-RHY-1 with the sun elevation the simulation already computes.

targets.metric: Start of night-nest building relative to sunset
targets.definition: Minutes between the start of night-nest building and sunset (positive = before sunset), median over individual-days.

field.value: weaned chimpanzees typically start night nests around 18:00; nest building often observed around sunset
field.method: statement in the introduction of a nest-building study

accept.basis: one general statement at an equatorial site, widened; no measured distribution was found

targets.notes: Weakly sourced. Clock times seen in search snippets for Toro-Semliki (19:09) and Fongoli (18:48) were not verified and are not used. How to measure: tick of the nest action start against the simulation's sunset.

targets.metric: Activity at night
targets.definition: Share of out-of-nest activity records (travel, feeding, social) that fall between dusk and dawn.

field.value: 1.80% of chimpanzee camera-trap activity is nocturnal; at 18 of 22 sites; mostly in twilight hours
3.3% of forest clips at night (41.8% at maize fields)

accept.basis: up to the Kibale forest value with a margin

targets.notes: Guards the E2 night-safety test: removing the night menu must not produce night foraging. How to measure: count ticks out of the nest and moving on the ground by hour of day (simulation truth); a camera-trap observer is not needed.

targets.metric: Drinking frequency
targets.definition: Drinking events (free water) per individual per 12 h of follow time, adult females; dry against wet months.

field.value: 788 drinks in 10,517 h of observation (0.075 per h, about 0.9 per 12 h, derived); 0.001 of observation minutes; more in the dry season

accept.basis: one site, drier than Kibale, widened about threefold downward and twofold upward

targets.notes: Also direction: more drinking in dry months. Never set: thirst comes from the water balance. How to measure: count drink actions on focal follows of adult females; divide by follow hours.

targets.metric: Share of drinking at streams
targets.definition: Share of all drinking events that take place at running water.

field.value: 3,102 of 4,087 drinking events at streams (76%); tree and buttress holes 382; puddles and footprints 511; 625 with a tool

accept.basis: one site, ± about 15 points

targets.notes: Scorable only if water sources carry a kind (stream, puddle, tree hole). How to measure: all-occurrence drink events by the kind of water source.

targets.metric: Rest and ground use rise with heat
targets.definition: Association between the share of scans resting (and the share on the ground) and air temperature at the scan, within hours of the day and across days.

field.value: resting and terrestriality both positively correlated with temperature in the sun; time in the sun falls from about 30 °C and sharply at about 40 °C; ground use 26.5% (F), 41.5% (M)
field.method: 5-min records with shade and sun temperature

field.value: ground use 23.4% of time (2.9% to 42.1% by month); rises with the day's maximum temperature

accept.basis: positive association of resting with temperature; midday rest follows from the temperature curve

targets.notes: Today the midday rest literal and a temperature bonus encode this; it counts as validation only with both removed (E2). How to measure: pair each 5-min focal sample with the weather temperature of that tick; logistic regression of resting on temperature with hour of day as a covariate.

targets.metric: Hourly activity profile
targets.definition: Feeding and resting shares by hour of the active day.

field.value: feeding peaks early and late in the day with rest around midday: widely described; no verified quantitative source was reached in this pass
field.note: only the heat-rest relation is sourced

accept.basis: feeding share in the first and last three hours of the active day above the middle hours; resting highest in the middle third

targets.notes: Low confidence: register only when a primary source with hourly values is added. How to measure: existing 1-min focal samples binned by hour since nest departure.

targets.metric: Leaf feeding later in the day
targets.definition: Share of leaf-feeding minutes that fall in the second half of the active day.

field.value: leaves of two sapling species eaten more in the evening than in the morning; leaf sugars higher and fibre lower in the evening

accept.basis: more than half of leaf feeding in the second half of the active day

targets.notes: The field cause is leaf chemistry changing through the day, which the simulation does not model; a pass would have to come from fruit being eaten first. How to measure: focal feeding minutes on leaves by half of the active day.

targets.metric: Male stress rises when the hierarchy is unstable
targets.definition: Stress reading of adult males in months with rank reversals among adult males against months without, within males; and by rank.

field.value: higher in unstable periods, more so at higher rank (interaction 0.122, SE 0.044); hierarchy unstable on 35% of days; 145 rank reversals
higher in all males in unstable periods, although aggression rates were lower then

accept.basis: stress higher in unstable than in stable periods

targets.notes: Informative only if instability is not wired to the stress state directly. How to measure: sample the stress state at simulated urinations (the 135-270 min urinary lag can be applied as a delay); classify months by Elo reversals from the observer's pant-grunt record.

targets.metric: Male stress and rank
targets.definition: Association between mean stress reading and Elo rank among adult males.

field.value: rises with rank (estimate 0.494, SE 0.168); no separate alpha effect
positive correlation with rank in a stable hierarchy
no association
no association (faecal cortisol)

accept.basis: not negative: high-ranking males are not less stressed than low-ranking males

targets.notes: Sites disagree, so only the weak form is registered. How to measure: mean stress reading per adult male over a year against its Elo rank.

targets.metric: Male stress with parous oestrous females present
targets.definition: Stress reading of adult males on days with a maximally swollen parous female in the party against other days.

field.value: higher with parous oestrous females present (estimate 0.176, SE 0.013, P < 0.001), across ranks

accept.basis: higher with a swollen parous female in the party

targets.notes: How to measure: stress samples split by the party-scan record of swollen parous females.

targets.metric: Stress after an aggressive interaction
targets.definition: Ratio of the stress reading 135-270 min after an aggressive interaction to the reading before it, against the same ratio around a rest of more than 30 min; aggressors and victims.

field.value: 112% ± 28 after aggression against 85% ± 27 after resting; probably for aggressors and victims; larger rise at higher rank; no effect of length or intensity

accept.basis: relative level after aggression above the level after rest, for both roles

targets.notes: Likely ENCODED once E4 lets aggression drive the stress state; flag it at registration if so. How to measure: read the stress state before the event and 135-270 min after it.

targets.metric: Stress is lower with a bond partner
targets.definition: Relative stress reading after grooming, resting and intergroup encounters, split by whether the partner (or supporter) was a bond partner.

field.value: 23% lower with a bond partner across all three contexts; almost 22% higher after intergroup encounters than after grooming; more than 8% higher after resting than after grooming

accept.basis: lower with bond partners in every context; intergroup encounters above grooming

targets.notes: How to measure: bond partners from the observer's association and grooming network; stress read before and after each event.

targets.metric: Female stress, food and rank
targets.definition: Stress reading of lactating females in low-fruit against high-fruit months, and against rank.

field.value: lactating females higher in months of low fruit consumption; low rank higher, most of all in lactation; oestrous females higher after male aggression; rises with age

accept.basis: lactating females higher in low-fruit months; low-ranking lactating females higher than high-ranking ones

targets.notes: For males the food effect is disputed within Kanyawara (mullerWrangham2004a negative; muller2021 none), so no male row is proposed. How to measure: stress samples of lactating females by month against the phenology index and female rank.

targets.metric: Competitive arousal with parous oestrous females
targets.definition: Competitive-arousal reading of adult males in parties with a swollen parous female, with a swollen nulliparous female, and with none; also against party size.

field.value: urinary testosterone above baseline with parous oestrous females, not with nulliparous ones; not explained by mating or by large parties; rank had no influence
same pattern (secondary summaries)

accept.basis: above baseline with parous swollen females; not above baseline with nulliparous ones or in large parties without them

targets.notes: How to measure: arousal samples split by party-scan composition.

targets.metric: Competitive arousal and pant-hoot rate
targets.definition: Association between a male's hourly competitive-arousal reading and his pant-hoots per hour; and between monthly means.

field.value: hourly testosterone positively associated with hourly pant-hoot rate; monthly levels with monthly rates, controlling for fission-fusion rate

accept.basis: positive association

targets.notes: How to measure: arousal state per hour against the focal's pant-hoot count from the call log.

targets.metric: Competitive arousal on patrol days
targets.definition: Competitive-arousal reading of adult males on patrol days against non-patrol days.

field.value: testosterone reported higher on patrols (seen only as cited by others; a summary gives about 25% above mean for testosterone and cortisol)

accept.basis: higher on patrol days

targets.notes: Not verified against the paper or its abstract. Patrols are the last behaviour E4 touches; this row must not be used to design the patrol mechanism. How to measure: arousal samples on days the patrol classifier marks against other days.

targets.metric: Affiliation after grooming with a bond partner
targets.definition: Affiliation reading after a grooming bout with a bond partner, with a non-bond partner, and after no grooming.

field.population: wild chimpanzees (site not in the abstract)
field.value: urinary oxytocin higher after grooming with bond partners than with non-bond partners or after no grooming, whatever the relatedness; not explained by grooming duration or direction

accept.basis: bond partner above non-bond partner and above no grooming

targets.notes: Likely ENCODED if E4 makes grooming with a bond partner feed the affiliation state; flag it at registration if so. How to measure: read the affiliation state after each grooming bout; bond status from the observer's network.

targets.metric: Affiliation after food sharing
targets.definition: Affiliation reading after a food-sharing event, after social feeding without sharing, and after grooming.

field.population: wild chimpanzees (site not in the abstract)
field.value: urinary oxytocin higher after food sharing than after other social feeding, whatever the prior bond, and higher than after grooming

accept.basis: sharing above social feeding and above grooming

targets.notes: Likely ENCODED if sharing feeds the affiliation state directly. How to measure: read the affiliation state after each sharing event in the event log.

targets.metric: Affiliation before and during intergroup conflict
targets.definition: Affiliation reading before and during patrols and intergroup encounters against control periods, both sexes.

field.value: urinary oxytocin higher before and during intergroup conflict in both sexes; linked to cohesion, not to threat level
higher after reconciliation and bystander affiliation than after aggression alone

accept.basis: higher before and during intergroup conflict than in control periods

targets.notes: A correlate, not a cause (research.md, patrols section). How to measure: affiliation state in the hour before and during classified patrols and encounters against matched control hours.
